reply:
INT holds a maximum of 2,147,483,647 — 10 digits, not 12. The (11) is purely a display width hint for ZEROFILL; it doesn't affect the actual storage limit.

For 12-digit numbers, you need BIGINT (64-bit signed, up to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807) or DECIMAL/NUMERIC with explicit precision like DECIMAL(12,0).

grade.note: Assistant now agrees INT is 32-bit with 10-digit max and (11) is just a display width hint, matching ground truth.
